title: Pregnancy Trimesters for Fathers
description: In this video, learn about what to expect your partner to experience throughout pregnancy.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about pregnancy trimesters for fathers.
transcript: Trimesters explained for fathers and what to expect here are a few things you can expect your partner to experience throughout the pregnancy during the first trimester your partner may experience morning sickness however this could happen at night as well the biggest change is that your partner will need more rest during this period during the second trimester your partner's body has adjusted to being pregnant so her energy levels improve morning sickness usually goes away and she typically feels better physically as well during the third trimester your partner may experience discomfort have trouble sleeping and have trouble doing routine tasks since your body is now getting ready for birth [Music] the next step is labor which is between 10 to 20 hours and occurs in three stages it's important to note that during an emergency you may be asked to leave the room just know that if they can't tell you in the moment it is because they must act quickly and someone will explain it to you later during labor your support is so helpful and extremely beneficial to your partner so don't forget that your role during all of this is important too.

title: Pregnancy Trimesters
description: Learn about the three pregnancy trimesters and what to expect in each trimester.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about pregnancy trimesters.
transcript: Pregnancy in trimesters a pregnancy is divided into three trimesters you will encounter different experiences at each stage in your pregnancy each trimester is about 12 to 14 weeks and a full-term pregnancy lasts about 40 weeks here are some of the things you can expect in each trimester the first trimester is from 0 to 13 weeks you'll experience many hormonal changes the baby's body and organs develop you'll have morning sickness Cravings or food aversions fatigue sore breasts frequent urination and this is a crucial time period for baby development the second trimester is 14 to 26 weeks most of the unpleasant symptoms will go away you'll experience increased energy and better sleep back pain constipation leg cramps stretch marks swollen ankles face and fingers baby's first movements and you may be able to do your ultrasound to determine the gender third trimester is 27 to 40 weeks this is the last stretch of pregnancy you may experience excitement and nervousness for the birth shortness of breath urinary incontinence or leaking sleeping issues leaky breasts and contractions remember that each women's experiences are different your trimesters may play out differently from what another expecting mother is experiencing your trimesters may even be different from one pregnancy to the next.

title: Signs of Pregnancy
description: Learn some of the common symptoms of early pregnancy.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about signs of pregnancy.
transcript: Signs you might be pregnant a missed period This is a common sign of early pregnancy if it has been more than a week since you expected your period you might be pregnant however this is not a sure sign as some women have an irregular period swollen and tender breasts hormonal changes that come with pregnancy may cause sore and swollen breasts early on nausea and vomiting you may know this as morning sickness which is nausea that occurs due to pregnancy though it is called morning sickness it can occur at any time of the day frequent urination pregnancy causes the amount of fluid in your body to increase resulting in more frequent urination fatigue if you're sleepier than usual throughout the day it could be a sign of pregnancy these are all common symptoms of early pregnancy but they are not 100 identifiers the best way to know if you are pregnant is to take a pregnancy test.

title: Preparing for Labor
description: Learn about how to prepare for giving birth as you come upon your due date.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about preparing for labor.
transcript: How to prepare for giving birth being pregnant can cause a lot of stress you may be worried about your baby your job your family and more a great thing you could do to ease your stress as you come upon your due date is to prepare yourself for labor eat nutritious Foods fueling your body with healthy foods leading up to childbirth will Aid in keeping you and your baby healthy this can include lean meats fish whole grains fruits nuts and veggies move your body being pregnant can make it hard to work out but there are many mental and physical benefits that come with exercise labor itself is hard work and if you engage in regular exercise leading up to labor your body will be strong and well equipped for childbirth this can include walking swimming yoga Pilates and other low impact exercises take a child birth class this is a wonderful way to learn more about what to expect so you feel more confident going into labor there are many different types of classes available ranging from breathing techniques to newborn care rest get seven to eight hours of sleep per night especially leading up to labor mindset goes a long way so being mindful or practicing deep breathing exercises can help you feel relaxed during labor pack your hospital bag labor can come on so quickly and unexpectedly so having a bag packed can assist in removing some of the stress this can include items such as outfits for you your partner and your baby maybe a phone charger any necessary identification documents snacks toiletries and more stock up on groceries and household items your newborn baby will be keeping you busy and the last thing you'll want to do is go on a grocery run ask questions you'll feel more at ease if you're not worried about a bunch of different things talk to your doctor or childbirth class instructors it is good to have a general plan going into labor but things may not go exactly how you expect what is important is that mother and baby are happy and healthy so don't let the little thing stress you out too much foreign.

title: Maternal Anexity
description: Learn about recognizing and preventing maternal anxiety.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about maternal anxiety.
transcript: Maternal anxiety recognition and prevention you've probably heard of postpartum depression but what about postpartum anxiety it's real but not talked about very much how can you tell if you're concerned about your newborn or if you have maternal anxiety how much worrying is too much worrying what is maternal anxiety maternal anxiety occurs during and after pregnancy it's excessive worrying racing thoughts bad feelings and Dread some worry is natural during pregnancy or after giving birth but these worries should not be severe and will eventually go away it becomes a problem when they do not go away or are irrational does this only present after the baby is born not necessarily it can occur during pregnancy as well during pregnancy this may present as excessive worry throughout it you may ask yourself is my baby's heart beating is my baby healthy feeling them kick or move around and hearing their heartbeat does not ease the worry Is this different from postpartum depression they are different but they commonly go hand in hand depression is Extreme sadness while anxiety is Extreme worry women are at a higher risk of developing maternal anxiety if they've dealt with anxiety in the past these feelings can be caused by not only a history of anxiety but also by hormones a history of depression and a history of miscarriage or infant loss ways to cope with maternal anxiety maternal anxiety presents in up to 20 percent of women a spouse can also experience parental anxiety even if they did not birth the baby ways to cope include therapy meditation exercise healthy distractions and medication from a provider if you have any concerns contact your health care provider foreign.

title: Foods to Avoid
description: Learn about food to avoid consuming during pregnancy.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about foods to avoid when pregnant.
transcript: Foods to avoid while pregnant [Music] when you're pregnant you're eating for two and one of those two are your developing baby it's important to know what foods should not be consumed during pregnancy and why first up is undercooked meat and undercooked Seafood as a pregnant mother you're going to want to avoid these because they may contain dangerous bacteria toxoplasmosis is a blood infection and salmonella is a type of food poisoning each of these can cause dangerous complications in your pregnancy shellfish is the most common cause of seafood-borne illnesses this can include oysters clams mussels shrimp and lobster these Foods may contain dangerous algae that should not be consumed at any time and especially not during pregnancy have you ever heard people say not to eat raw cookie dough well this is especially important when you're pregnant raw eggs or foods that contain them are not recommended for expecting mothers due to the salmonella risk watch out for homemade mayonnaise custards and ice cream these Foods tend to be safe when bought from a grocery store because pasteurized products are used so just be weary of homemade foods Brie feta Camembert Gorgonzola and other soft cheeses may contain a bacteria called listeria listeria can cross the placenta and infect your baby which can be life-threatening you should always check to make sure the cheeses you're eating were made with pasteurized milk following that you should never consume unpasteurized milk or dairy products some types of fish contain high levels of mercury which is a substance that has been linked to fetal development issues during pregnancy examples include swordfish king mackerel and some tuna canned tuna has a lower amount of mercury than other Tunas but it should still be eaten in moderation deli meat is another food that is commonly contaminated with listeria if you're really craving a ham or turkey sandwich you can thoroughly cook the deli meat on a stove to kill the bacteria it's not that you can't eat veggies you're actually highly encouraged to they're a great source of fiber just make sure you thoroughly wash those veggies that you get from the grocery store because if not they can be dangerous for your baby this is because they may be carrying toxoplasmosis from the soil that they are grown in be wary of pre-packaged veggie trays from the store and raw veggies from somewhere other than your kitchen no amount of alcohol should be consumed during pregnancy if a baby is exposed to alcohol they're subject to developmental issues it can also cause fetal alcohol syndrome which can harm your child alcohol should also be avoided during breastfeeding and that is it those are some of the foods that should be avoided throughout your pregnancy to assist with the Healthy Growth of your baby.

title: Father of a Premature Baby
description: In this video, learn about what to expect as the father to a premature baby.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about being a father of a premature baby.
transcript: What to expect as a father of a premature baby as a father you may feel mixed emotions about this experience joy as well as fear for some of the unknown challenges you may also feel overwhelmed at times the important thing to remember is that this is completely natural it's healthy for you to take the time to think about these emotions and your needs take a shower go on a walk take a quick nap do whatever you need to do in order to acknowledge these feelings and take care of yourself this will lead you to having more energy to care for your partner and baby as well being a part of your baby's care is another way to bond with your child and help with this whole process helping with feeding bathing or changing are all easy ways to get involved talk to the hospital staff if you ever feel left out and they can help another thing to note is that you may have extra responsibilities while your child is in the NICU such as making trips to the hospital while also balancing grocery shopping going to work and taking care of other children [Music] this can be overwhelming for anyone so remember it is okay to get help talk to your partner family members or friends to get the support you may need during this time.

title: Exercise After Birth
description: In this video, learn about the benefits and types of postpartum exercise.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about exercise after birth.
transcript: What to know about exercise after giving birth after giving birth it may be difficult to get into a workout routine but there are many benefits that exercise can bring in the postpartum period here are some of the benefits it can strengthen abdominal and lower back muscles promote better sleep aid and stress relief improve your mood raise energy levels improve your heart health help to prevent postpartum depression and can help to lose extra weight gained while pregnant your doctor should always be consulted when you're planning to begin exercising as clearance to exercise can depend on many individual factors in general you should be able to begin exercising once you feel comfortable enough to do so an example of this would be going on walks six weeks after birth tends to be when your body returns to normal after the changes that came with pregnancy this might be different for women who had a cesarean birth or complications when giving birth remember to take it slow and listen to your body begin with low impact exercises and gradually work up to higher intensities stop exercising if you feel any pain it is suggested that people get 150 minutes of exercise per week which could be split into 30 minutes a day for 5 days here are some workouts that you could try walking swimming yoga Pilates lightweight training and cycling foreign.

title: C-Section vs. Vaginal Birth
description: Learn about differences between cesarean births and vaginal births.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about C-sections vs. vaginal births.
transcript: Cesarean birth versus vaginal birth if you are expecting a baby you may have wondered whether a cesarean birth or a C-section or a vaginal birth is the best choice for you it is very important to be educated on each of these options so you can make the best decision for you and your baby usually vaginal birth is safer than a C-section for most women and babies however in some instances a C-section is the only safe option depending on the baby's positioning and other factors you might be wondering what a C-section is a C-section is when a baby is delivered through a surgical incision made through the abdomen and the uterus some benefits to a C-section would be that it is a safer option for you than a vaginal birth your provider May recommend it depending on your situation an example of this is when the baby is positioned feet or bottom first harms of a C-section include longer recovery time than vaginal birth this is a surgical procedure so there are risks of infection and serious bleeding C-sections can cause chronic pain for the mother and babies are at increased risk of childhood diseases such as asthma benefits to vaginal birth include the fact that it is easier on the body than a C-section the bacteria that the baby is exposed to Aid in decreasing the chance that the baby will have chronic diseases in the future harms of vaginal birth are that the vaginal tissue can stretch and tear most of the time these are minor and can heal but sometimes they are more severe this can also cause bladder and bowel weakness so there can be leakage after giving birth one thing to know is that if you have a C-section for one baby you will need to birth all of your following babies the same way if you wish for more information about Which choice is best for you and your situation reach out to your provider they will help you to become informed so you can make a decision.

title: Pregnancy Cravings
description: Learn about cravings and how to proceed with pregnancy cravings.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about pregnancy cravings.
transcript: Pregnancy cravings pregnancy cravings are when you have a strong desire to eat a certain food the Cravings could be very common foods or they could be Foods you don't typically enjoy [Music] Additionally you may begin to dislike certain foods that have strong flavors or smells it is okay to give in to the Cravings as long as it's done in moderation be careful with sugary Cravings though as too much could lead to excessive weight gain dental problems or make gestational diabetes worse here are a few tips to manage the Cravings regular healthy meals can prevent sudden moments of hunger as well as eating low glycemic index foods which will keep you feeling full and energized for longer drinking lots of water helps too something else to be aware of is a condition called Pika which means craving dirt Clay and other non-food items if you are experiencing these non-food Cravings talk to your doctor or health care provider just to ensure everything in your body is balanced.

title: Breastmilk Pumping and Storing
description: Learn about how to pump and store breastmilk for your baby.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about breastmilk pumping and storing.
transcript: Breast milk pumping and storing if you breastfeed you may find it difficult to leave your baby without worrying about them getting fed whether you're going to work going on a trip or just having your partner help with feeding you're going to want to have breast milk stored and available to achieve this you may want to pump and store your breast milk but you might not know where to start if you're pumping your breast milk and you're away from your baby it would be helpful to pump during the times that your baby would normally eat so that your body continues making milk wash your hands thoroughly and make sure your pump parts are clean along with the area that you are pumping if you are having trouble getting milk flowing you could try gently massaging your breasts or try to relax after pumping you can keep milk at room temperature for up to four hours refrigerate it for up to four days freeze it put it in a cooler or use a cooler pack for up to 24 hours there are breast milk storing bags that you can buy which are specifically made for freezing breast milk good practice for storing breast milk includes labeling containers with the date freezing in small amounts leaving a room at the top of the container for the milk to expand when freezing and storing milk in the back of the freezer so it stays Frozen good practice for thawing and warming breast milk includes thawing the older milk first thawing it in the fridge overnight warming the bag under warm water never put breast milk in the microwave test milk temperatures on the wrist to avoid burning your baby use within 24 hours of thawing in the fridge and do not refreeze after thawing if you have any questions or concerns about breastfeeding and pumping contact your nurse Midwife or pediatrician for guidance.

title: Baby Led Weaning
description: Learn about what baby led weaning is and how to begin baby led weaning.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about baby led weaning.
transcript: Baby lead weaning around six months of age your pediatrician may suggest adding solid foods to your baby's diet traditionally this would include pureed and mushy foods in order to Aid digestion and prevent choking but baby lead weaning is an increasingly popular alternative to feeding your baby baby LED weaning is a practice where babies of six months or older skip pureed and mashed foods and begin eating age-appropriate finger foods as soon as solids are introduced essentially this includes your baby feeding themselves the nutritious foods that they want right from the beginning they will learn how to gum or chew food swallow bring food to their mouth and eat till they're full when parents feed their baby they tend to spoon more food into the baby's mouth than the baby may be hungry for which can lead to a habit of the child ignoring feelings of fullness and eating more than necessary baby lead weaning prevents this as the baby can self-regulate the amount of food they eat and may result in a lower chance of overeating and becoming overweight another benefit of baby lead weaning is that it allows babies to experience a large variety of textures and flavors this may lead to healthy varied diets later in life along with a lower chance of food allergies some downsides are that baby LED weaning is Messy as your child will be grabbing foods with their hands and learning how to get it to their mouth another concern is that you need to pay attention to the foods that they're eating in order to ensure that they are consuming the necessary amounts of vitamins such as iron tips for baby lead weaning keep the food soft enough to smush or easily dissolved cut the food so it's easy for them to grab eat with your baby so they can mimic you give them the same Foods you're eating offer a variety of foods and continue to nurse or bottle feed at the same time of course you may be concerned about your baby choking on Foods here are some tips to make you feel more secure avoid choking hazard foods like whole Grapes apple slices large chunks of foods and crunchy snacks supervise them all they eat keep them sitting up looking for allergic reactions and take an infant CPR class take it slow and have fun with it you may find it useful to research the best foods for baby LED weaning so you can find soft or dissolvable Foods as they get older they'll be more ready for hard chewable Foods if you have any concerns consult your doctor.

title: Allergies
description: Learn about allergic reactions and your baby.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about food allergies in babies and young children.
transcript: Allergies in your baby as a parent you're constantly worrying about your child one thing you may often worry about when they begin eating Foods is allergies allergic reactions can seem scary but learning more about what to expect can allow you to be better prepared an allergy is an overreaction of the body to a food or substance in the environment also known as an allergen the cause is not clear but it might be genetic so if you or your partner have allergies your child is at higher risk of having them as well [Music] food allergies can start as soon as food is introduced for the first time environmental allergies likely will not begin until 18 months of age common food allergies in young children include milk eggs fish and shellfish wheat soy and nuts [Music] symptoms of food allergies may include skin rashes hives wheezing congestion and digestive issues many children outgrow food allergies by age five as the immune system matures fish shellfish and nut allergies tend to continue later in life [Music] common environmental allergies in young children include dust mites outdoor pollens molds pets and cockroaches symptoms of environmental allergies may include itchy eyes and nose congestion sneezing coughing and Asthma these allergies are less likely to be outgrown as the child grows if you suspect that your child has an allergy visit your child's doctor they can run some tests and help you figure out how to treat your child's symptoms.

title: Breastfeeding vs. Formula Feeding
description: Learn about the differences between breastfeeding and formula feeding.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about breastfeeding vs. formula feeding.
transcript: Breastfeeding versus Formula feeding with parenting comes a lot of decisions to be made about your baby one of these is deciding between breastfeeding or formula feeding experts believe that breastfeeding is the healthier option if possible however there are some health issues that make it impossible for women to breastfeed breastfeeding is not recommended if you are infected with HIV you are undergoing radiation therapy you are taking medications that can harm your baby if passed through breast milk always check with your provider if you have any questions benefits to breastfeeding include skin-to-skin contact allowing bonding it's convenient milk is absorbed well by the baby antibodies and nutrients can be passed on from the mother can help the baby fight infection easy for the baby to digest no cost and it helps the mother's body return to pre-pregnancy State quicker drawbacks to breastfeeding are that it can be uncomfortable or painful for mother large time commitment baby can't be fed by anyone else unless mother pumps mother has to watch diet as substances can pass to baby benefits to formula feeding are that someone other than the mother can feed it's available at any time rather than waiting for the body to make milk no need to seek privacy when feeding mother does not need to watch the diet and there's no need to feed as often since formula is digested slower drawbacks to formula feeding are that no antibodies are passed on must plan ahead and have formula in stock must have a way to warm formula it can be costly and it's not as easily digested but it is still a nutritious option it is recommended that moms try to breastfeed for the first six months then continue feeding the baby breast milk in addition to food after that if possible try to breastfeed your baby as much as you can and then you can supplement with formula if they need more milk both breastfeeding and baby formula are nutritious options for your baby the most important thing is that they are happy and healthy so just do what you can and do your best.

title: Bodily Changes During Pregnancy
description: Learn about body changes that occur during pregnancy.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about bodily changes during pregnancy.
transcript: How the body changes during pregnancy some bodily changes throughout pregnancy are obvious but some are more subtle nearly every bodily system goes through changes and many body parts do as well let's take a look at how the endocrine system is also known as the hormone system throughout pregnancy your body will be flooded with hormones and here are some changes you may notice as a result moodiness High emotions exhaustion nausea and hot flashes this is all due to various hormones the amount of blood in your body will increase to support your baby resulting in increased work for your kidneys and urinary system there's an increased risk for varicose veins and hemorrhoids dizziness and fainting frequent urination elevated heart rate and urinary leakage when sneezing coughing or laughing as your baby grows more pressure will be put on the stomach and intestines leading to changes in digestion you may experience constipation acid reflux heartburn or slow digestion try to combat this by eating smaller meals more frequently throughout pregnancy your spine will realign to maintain balance your posture and gait may change in response it's not uncommon to experience back pain during pregnancy because of these changes around the time that labor will begin the pelvic bones will begin to loosen up you will need a larger amount of oxygen for the growth of your baby as a result you may experience to increased respiratory rate shortness of breath increased amount of rest needed when exercising and respiratory alkalosis breasts will change due to the hormones estrogen and progesterone here are some of the changes increase size tender breasts nipples may stick out colostrum leaking from nipples in the third trimester this is allowing your body to prepare for feeding your baby the abdomen expands greatly during the second and third trimester by the end of pregnancy the uterus will have expanded so much that it will reach the rib cage due to stretching a mother may experience her abdomen aching there may also be an appearance of stretch marks on the abdomen as well as the thighs breasts and buttocks other changes may include leg cramps blurred vision sciatica changes in hair and nail growth swollen feet and ankles and a slight increase in body temperature on average a woman will gain 25 to 35 pounds throughout her pregnancy in order to support her baby the body undergoes many changes in order to grow a baby though some may be unpleasant try to find comfort in knowing that your body is adapting in order to create the best possible environment for your baby.

title: Braxton Hicks Contractions
description: Learn about Braxton Hicks contractions.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about Braxton Hicks contractions.
transcript: Understanding Braxton Hicks contractions Braxton Hicks contractions are the intermittent tightening of your abdomen your uterus is Contracting to prepare for birth however they don't cause labor or signify that labor is starting it feels like the muscles of your belly are tight and your uterus spills hard it is uncomfortable but they should not be painful and they last about 30 seconds they occur early on but you most likely won't feel them until the second trimester however pre-labor occurs when your body is preparing for labor during late pregnancy the contractions may occur every 10 to 20 minutes at this stage here are a few of the major differences between Braxton Hicks and true labor contractions for Braxton Hicks they are irregular last 30 seconds and usually stop if you go for a walk on the other hand true labor contractions are regular start getting close together last 30 to 70 seconds and can get stronger if you walk call your doctor or Midwife If you experience pain the contractions are regular stronger and closer together or if fluid is leaking from your vagina if you feel uncomfortable during the contractions try lying down going for a walk taking a warm bath or getting a massage.

title: Baby Teething
description: Learn tips for when your baby begins teething.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about baby teething.
transcript: Baby teething what is teething teething is when a baby is first getting their teeth and they are coming through their gums it can be a hard painful time for baby which can make it a hard time for their parents as well let's talk about what to expect so you can be best prepared to help your baby when will it start you will most likely see their teeth poking through their gums at about four to seven months of age the first ones to appear will likely be the bottom two front teeth followed by the Upper Front Teeth the molars will be the last to appear and your child should have all of their teeth by the time they are three years old signs of teething drooling more wanting to chew on things being irritated or cranky crying and sleep and eating is disrupted some babies have no pain when teething they should not have a fever or diarrhea so if this occurs contact your doctor how to make it easier for baby rub their gums with a clean finger give them something safe to chew on like a teething ring ask your doctor about baby pain medications and do not rub alcohol on their gums how to care for their teeth daily Dental Care brush gently with an infant toothbrush and a tiny amount of toothpaste brush their teeth twice a day once all their teeth are in include flossing into their routine don't let your baby fall asleep with a bottle in their mouth and see a dentist at age one.

title: Bathing Your Baby
description: Learn about common concerns when bathing your baby.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about bathing your baby.
transcript: Bathing your baby with a new baby comes anxiety about many things bathing may seem so natural to you yet once you have a newborn you might not know where to begin here are some commonly asked questions about bathing your baby when should my baby have their first bath it is recommended that you wait 24 hours after the baby's birth to give them their first bath this is done to prevent hypothermia and a sudden drop in blood sugar that can come with the stress of a bath it can also disrupt skin to skin bonding finally babies have a waxy substance on their body called burnix that acts as a natural moisturizer it would be ideal to not wash this away prematurely so the baby's skin doesn't dry out how often should my baby be bathed newborn babies don't really get dirty so they shouldn't require a bath every day giving them a bath too often could dry out their skin bathing your baby three times a week should be enough how to give a sponge bath a sponge bath should be used until the stump of the umbilical cord falls off about two weeks after birth you'll need a basin of water a washcloth and a towel lay your baby on a comfortable surface start by washing their face and continue on to the rest of their body ending with their bottom make sure to keep your baby warm throughout the bath and dry them off well when can I give my baby a regular bath once their umbilical area is healed you can start giving them a regular bath be very gentle and work as quickly and safely as possible you can use an infant tub or a sink always check the water temperature and make sure it's warm not hot never leave them alone and try having one hand on them at all times to ensure that they are safe moments like bathing your baby are very special try to enjoy it and don't stress about it too much just remember all the basics thank you.

title: Can You Get Pregnant on Your Period
description: Learn about how pregnancy relates to your period.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about getting pregnant on your period.
transcript: Can you get pregnant on your period it is not likely that you will get pregnant if you have sex while on your period this is because ovulation which is the time that a woman is most likely to conceive is several days after your period this applies to women who have the typical 28 to 30 day cycle the exception is women who have a shorter cycle around 21 to 24 days these women can ovulate soon after their period And since sperm can live inside you for up to five days there is a chance that you could become pregnant what about right after your period right after your period you are approaching your fertility window again sperm can live up to five days inside a human body if you have sex right before your period there is a chance that you could become pregnant your chances of conceiving increases with every day after your period has ended what about right before your period the chance of getting pregnant right before your period is very low if you have a normal cycle you will likely ovulate sometime between day 11 and day 21. an egg is only available for 12 to 24 hours to be fertilized this means that the days right before your period are the safest time to have sex without getting pregnant women's ovulation Cycles vary so chances can be different for everyone if you are trying to conceive the best chances are in the later days of your cycle if you are not trying to conceive the earlier days are safer but you should also use another form of birth control like condoms or a pill.

title: Pregnancy Weight Fluctuations
description: Learn about how much weight gain can be too much during pregnancy.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about pregnancy weight fluctuations.
transcript: During pregnancy how much weight gain is too much if your BMI is considered normal which is between 18.5 and 24.9 the recommendation is to gain between 25 and 35 pounds gain a little more if you're underweight and a little less if you're overweight here are a few tips in order to get your weight back on track if you are over the recommendation don't dye it your baby needs the nutrients so now is not the time to diet in order to lose weight Instead try cutting out empty calories some examples would be substituting one or two percent milk instead of whole milk fresh fruit over dried fruit grilled chicken over fried chicken baked potatoes over french fries remember that you still need the calories these are just ideas of smart substitutions try getting active 30 minutes of exercise a day is recommended try incorporating exercise into your daily routine such as adding extra steps in your walk from your car to the store try to stop late night snacking eat smaller meals more frequently throughout the day and if you are going to eat snacks in the evening try to keep them light and nutritious what are some of the risks of gaining too much weight ultrasound results can be less accurate you can also experience increased blood pressure and increase discomfort you can experience preeclampsia or gestational diabetes or you could have preterm Labor or a larger baby during birth remember it is possible to control weight gain by talking to your doctor and using their help to modify your diet and add exercise into your daily routine.

title: In Vitro Fertilization (IVF)
description: Learn about In Vitro Fertilization as an option for pregnancy.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about in vitro fertilization (IVF).
transcript: Understanding in vitro fertilization if you've been struggling with infertility IVF may be another option for you how does it work during IVF eggs are fertilized by sperm outside of the body the fertilized eggs are then moved into the uterus and if one implants it will result in a pregnancy one cycle typically takes two weeks however you may need more than one cycle there are quite a few steps in the IVF process here is what you can expect some women may need to start with ovulation suppression by taking birth control it can suppress natural hormones to ensure IVF occurs at the right time the next step is hormone injections in order to stimulate the ovaries throughout this period you will need to monitor your hormone levels through regular blood tests and ultrasounds to determine how effective the injections are after 8 to 14 days you will then receive a trigger shot in order to help the eggs mature and to trigger ovulation the eggs will then be ready for retrieval 36 hours after the trigger shot the doctor will retrieve them transvaginally and it'll be done under IV sedation ensure someone can drive you back home after the procedure and be prepared to relax for the rest of the day the sperm are retrieved on the same day through either a sample previously frozen one or a donor sperm the next step is fertilization the eggs and sperm are fertilized in the lab and checked 12 to 14 hours later to see if it worked the embryos are monitored for the next few days and are genetically tested you will then be started on a progesterone boost in order to prepare your uterine lining for the embryo implantation the medication is continued through the first eight to ten weeks of pregnancy three to five days after the egg fertilization the embryo transfer occurs and the doctor will place the embryos in your uterus you are awake for the procedure and can oftentimes watch on an ultrasound monitor the last step would be getting a positive pregnancy test you will have a blood test two weeks after to determine if the IVF was successful how much does IVF cost a single cycle can be twelve thousand dollars there are additional costs for medication and other add-ons though which totals to fifteen thousand and twenty five thousand somewhere in between there it oftentimes takes more than one cycle so keep that in mind when determining the overall cost does insurance cover IVF 16 States currently mandate insurance coverage for infertility related treatments but many companies are starting to offer coverage or partial coverage for these treatments as well talk to your insurance company or employer to determine if it applies for you overall more than 270 000 IVF Cycles are done every year in the US and this results in over 74 000 babies being born so talk to your healthcare provider to determine if IVF is an option for you as well.

title: Risk Factors for Infertility
description: Learn about some risk factors for infertility.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about infertility.
transcript: Infertility what does it mean infertility is a disease characterized by the failure to establish a clinical pregnancy after 12 months of regular unprotected sexual intercourse or due to an impairment of a person's capacity to reproduce either as an individual or with his or her partner one of the first steps you can take is to consider talking to your health care provider about the possibility of infertility if you have Painful periods ovulation that can't be tracked more than one miscarriage history of STDs or an abnormal BMI you can start by researching fertility specialists near you being aware of some of the risk factors can allow you to make changes if needed here are a few of the ones that affect women overall health factors such as having too much or too little body fat chronic diseases such as diabetes lupus arthritis hyper or hypothyroidism hypertension or asthma abnormal pap smears hormone imbalances multiple miscarriages alcohol consumption or smoking as age increases risk for infertility increases as well talk to your health care provider if you are over 30 and have been trying to conceive for over six months STDs are another risk factor some of the following tips can help prevent them use latex condoms screen 4 and treat infections early and be aware that some STDs are asymptomatic fallopian tube diseases and endometriosis also affect fertility early detection is vital it runs in families so be sure to let your doctor know if there's any family history of these diseases depression and stress or other emotional factors can also impact your hormones and therefore your ability to conceive approximately 44 of women with infertility have sought medical assistance and of those who seek medical intervention approximately 65 percent give birth so reach out to your health care provider or fertility specialist if you think you may be having fertility struggles.

title: Insulin Use During Pregnancy
description: Learn about how to use insulin for diabetes during pregnancy.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about insulin use during pregnancy.
transcript: Insulin during pregnancy there are three types of diabetes type 1 diabetes is where your body doesn't make insulin type 2 is where your body makes insulin but you become resistant to it and in gestational diabetes your body becomes resistant to insulin and this occurs specifically during pregnancy insulin may be necessary to treat gestational diabetes if you have gestational diabetes you will need to learn how to check and monitor your blood sugar regularly here are the steps to give yourself an insulin injection first clean the site with alcohol or with soap and water then push the needle at a 90 degree angle into the site ensure the needle is all the way in then push the plunger down at a steady rate and pull the needle out during pregnancy your abdomen is the best spot to inject insulin the insulin gets into the bloodstream faster at this site be sure to make the injection two inches away from the belly button your arms and legs can be used as well if you can't use your abdomen the injection just needs to go into fatty tissue so you can inject it into the fleshy outer surface of your arm or into the top outer part of your leg just not the inner thigh know the signs of hypoglycemia your blood sugar is too low if it's under 60. symptoms include shaky sweating headache confused or blurry vision if your blood sugar is under 60 eat or drink 15 grams of carbohydrates some ideas can be fruit juice soda as long as it's not diet skim milk honey or four glucose tablets be sure to talk to your health care provider if you have questions or concerns related to your blood sugar.

title: Stretch Marks During Pregnancy
description: Learn about factors that effect stretch marks during pregnancy.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about stretch marks during pregnancy.
transcript: Understanding stretch marks what are stretch marks during pregnancy hormones can make the elastic fibers weaker leading them to snap as your belly grows factors that affect stretch marks can be hereditary or genetics or the rate at which your belly is growing when do they appear typically around the second trimester but again depends on how much weight you gain and how fast you gain what are some ways to prevent them you can try rubbing natural oils such as coconut oil or almond oil which will help moisturize your skin [Music] you should also drink lots of water as staying hydrated helps keep the elastic fibers flexible be careful with skin care products though and avoid essential oils or products that may irritate your skin or cause contractions do stretch marks go away the redness will fade after delivery and the marks themselves can also become less noticeable over time they can be a beautiful reminder of your body's amazing accomplishments talk to your doctor if you want more options to minimize them though.

title: Vaginal Discharge
description: Learn about different types of discharge and what they mean.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about vaginal discharge.
transcript: Vaginal discharge what the different types mean vaginal discharge is normal and can change throughout the menstrual cycle normal discharge is about a teaspoon per day that is white or transparent and odorless it can change depending on ovulation menstrual flow sexual activity and birth control before ovulation your body produces much more mucus than other times it is usually watery and stretchy during this time let's take a look at the different types of discharge and what they mean white discharge thick white discharge is common at the beginning and end of your cycle there should not be any type of itching if there is this could mean that you have a yeast infection and you should contact your provider clear discharge if it is stretchy this is known as fertile mucus and you are ovulating if it's watery this occurs normally at different times in the cycle this type of discharge might be especially Heavy after exercising yellow and green discharge May mean that there is an infection it may also have an irregular odor or a cottage cheese texture like thick and clumpy brown discharge you may experience brown discharge right after you end your period this is just your body cleaning itself out the brown color comes from the old blood mixing with your normal discharge spotting spotting is the presence of a small amount of light pink red or brown discharge this can occur when ovulating or maybe an early sign of pregnancy if you have spotting at the time when you are supposed to have your period you may want to take a pregnancy test when should you be concerned discharge can depend on your sexual partners birth control used and if abuse is involved see your provider if you have discharged that is yellow green clumpy or has a foul odor if you are having itching or Burning Sensations discomfort or rash or any sores associated with abnormal discharge see your doctor.

months for the shot take a prenatal vitamin prenatals help to prepare your body for baby having these vitamins in your body before conceiving will give you a boost as far as your baby's development some studies show that it can lower the risk of premature birth it is also believed that they can help you get pregnant faster increase Dairy and iron intake calcium increases the ability to produce healthy eggs and iron can help with regular Cycles calcium is found in Dairy like milk and cheese iron can Aid in regulating the menstrual cycles of anemic women which is a common condition that affects many women some foods rich in iron include leafy greens beans and lean meats like chicken decrease caffeine intake too much caffeine can discourage conception it is suggested that caffeine levels be limited to 200 milligrams or less per day alcohol is another substance that can seriously impact the chances of conceiving and it should be completely cut out of the diet the same goes for nicotine get a checkup your health care provider will be able to do a complete thorough head to toe assessment on you to screen for any conditions that can impact your chances of getting pregnant some of these disorders are ovarian cysts and hormonal imbalance they will also be able to identify any fertility issues that you could be having supplement your diet or your partner's diet healthy foods will increase your fertility and Aid in growing a healthy baby it helps if your partner eats well too healthy fats are good for both eggs and sperm this includes salmon walnuts and leafy greens other foods that help to create healthy sperm are fruits veggies oysters eggs dairy and nuts these have high amounts of vitamins a b and c as well as zinc and folate sleep not getting enough sleep is not good for anything and pregnancy is no exception if you are trying to get pregnant make sure you are getting seven to eight hours of sleep per night this can also help by decreasing your stress levels which increases your chances of getting pregnant finally try not to worry stress can lower chances of getting pregnant extreme levels of stress can cause hormonal imbalance which is not good for conception you can combat this by going to meditation or workout classes venting with a friend or lowering your workload.

title: Baby Acne
description: Learn about how to recognize and treat baby acne.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about baby acne.
transcript: Baby acne what it means and what to do about it what causes baby acne maternal hormones still in the bloodstream can stimulate the baby's oil producing glands which can lead to acne on their face neck back or chest additionally since their pores aren't developed completely they are at a higher risk for dirt to get inside they also have very sensitive skin here are a few tips to get rid of it make sure you leave the pimples alone so no picking or squeezing clean the area with warm water and Pat the skin dry gently and don't use soap for lotion a few more tips don't use adult skin products on your child use natural remedies instead such as using breast milk to dab on the area and ask your doctor for baby safe prescriptions if needed what's the difference between rashes and acne acne will look more like red pimples whereas some of these other common baby rashes have different appearances milia looks like small white bumps a heat rash is clusters of red bumps on their arms legs chest or face when it's hot outside diaper rash would be red irritated skin in the diaper area cradle cap is tiny red bumps with yellow flaky scaly skin associated with it and eczema would be dry flaky red patches that can spread to creases and turn into pimples with fluid inside them how long does baby acne last it can be from a few weeks after birth until the child is three to four months old there are no permanent scars though typically the baby acne will resolve on its own but make sure to call your doctor if the bumps appear infected which could be signs like extra redness swelling fluid leaking out of them or a fever and call your doctor if it seems like an allergic reaction is occurring too.

title: Breech Births
description: Learn important signs and symptoms of breech births.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about breech births.
transcript: Preach births things to know what is a breach birth before a baby is born during the last weeks of pregnancy they will reposition to where their head will come out first during birth this is also known as a Vertex presentation a breach presentation on the other hand is when the baby's bottom or feet are positioned to come out first during birth this is not very common but it can happen different types first is a complete breach the bottom is pointing downward with legs bent and the knees and feet near the baby's bottom then there is a frank breech this is where the bottom is aimed at the birth canal with the leg sticking straight up with the feet near the head finally there's a footling breach this is where the feet are pointing downward and will be delivered first some causes of breech birth it is not fully understood but it is thought that it is more common if you have been pregnant before there are multiple babies in the pregnancy there is a history of premature delivery there is an abnormally shaped uterus or the placenta is covering the opening of the uterus how can you tell if your baby is in a breached position in the weeks leading up to the due date the provider can place their hands on the mother's belly and may be able to tell if they are in a breached position from there they can do an ultrasound or a pelvic exam to confirm can it be changed there are some methods that can be used for turning a baby from the breech position into the vertex position it is recommended that you talk to your health care provider to see what method they recommend can I still do a vaginal delivery it is [Music] during delivery which impairs the delivery of oxygen and blood so Syrian delivery is usually the recommended method foreign

title: Kegel Exercises
description: Learn about the benefits of kegel exercises and tips to safely practice them.
infographic_description: In this infographic, learn about kegel exercises.
transcript: Kegel exercises Kegel exercises are also called pelvic floor exercises and they help to strengthen your lower abdominal muscles and your vaginal muscles these muscles support your uterus bladder intestines and bowels here are some of the benefits pregnant women who do kegels often have an easier birth kegels can help with bladder control and hemorrhoid prevention kegels help to reduce the chance of prolapse and they help to support the weight of the growing baby how to do kegel exercises first locate your pelvic floor muscles by inserting a finger into the vagina and squeezing the muscles around it once located contract for 5 to 10 seconds then relax repeat 10 to 20 times focusing only on the pelvic muscles refrain from overdoing it this may make you strain while using the bathroom you can do these exercises at any time you can do them when driving when in a waiting room when watching TV and so on you can expect results in a few weeks to a few months if you are doing them regularly don't be afraid to ask your provider for help if you're having trouble.
